Really? Did you notice his looks?
Of course, he likes you very much.
Then I will go to the bar counter.
Smile at him warmly and openly.
Max will definitely regret his behavior.
I wish you great luck, my friend!
Thanks for the support, dear Sasha!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'bar' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Вы можете подождать за барной стойкой.
examples.trans: You can wait at the bar counter.

examples.text: Что ты вообще делаешь за нашей барной стойкой?
examples.trans: What are you even doing behind our bar counter?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be afraid'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
Secondary conversational sense ('what if (in hypotheses)') (а вдруг... = what if...) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'гляд'). Common masculine noun meaning 'look, glance' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('view, opinion') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Really? Did you notice his looks?

examples.text: Настоящий талант всегда виден с первого взгляда.
examples.trans: Real talent is always visible at first sight.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to speak, to talk') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: with present: Я давно здесь = I've been here a long time
Secondary conversational sense ('long ago') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: + dative of person + genitive of thing: желаю вам удачи

examples.trans: Good health to you, sir! (I wish you health!)

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'мечать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to notice, observe', paired with 'заметить'.

examples.trans: Really? Did you notice his looks?

meanings.note: 'всё, что захотите' = everything you (may) want

examples.text: У вас будет всё, что захотите.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: praise, said to a man, woman or child
Secondary conversational sense ('a fine young man') (old-fashioned) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

examples.text: Молодец, Макс, ты сегодня отлично справился с горячим цехом!
examples.trans: Well done, Max, you handled the hot station brilliantly today!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'definitely'.

examples.trans: I'll definitely buy you a tank.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыто'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Smile at him warmly and openly.

examples.text: Ты просто нагло и открыто сейчас блефуешь!
examples.trans: You are simply insolently and openly bluffing now!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'first', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ведение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'behaviour, conduct' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She was fired for her conduct.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'держка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'support, backing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There you go! No support at all!
I really need the family's support.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'руга'). Common feminine noun meaning 'female friend, girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll invite a female friend over.

examples.text: Пять тысяч рублей. Я подругу приглашу.
examples.trans: Five thousand roubles. I'll invite a female friend over.

meanings.note: ты ещё пожалеешь! = you'll be sorry!
Secondary conversational sense ('to feel sorry for') (+ accusative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, сколько у меня денег? Ты ещё пожалеешь!
examples.trans: Do you know how much money I have? You'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to accept, to take') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'decision' in conversational and formal Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('solution') (to a problem) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I am forced to cancel my decision.
We have already made a decision.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to look', forming an aspectual pair with 'посмотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch') (TV, a film) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: almost always the short form: я согласен (man), я согласна (woman)

examples.text: Я полностью согласен с вашим предложением по новому меню!
examples.trans: I completely agree with your proposal for the new menu!

examples.text: Все повара были согласны остаться вечером и помочь шефу.
examples.trans: All the cooks agreed to stay in the evening and help the chef.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'counter'.

examples.text: Костя протёр барную стойку чистым полотенцем.
examples.trans: Kostya wiped the bar counter with a clean towel.

examples.text: Вы можете подождать за барной стойкой.
examples.trans: You can wait at the bar counter.

examples.text: Ты разлил молоко на всю стойку!
examples.trans: You spilled milk all over the counter!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'warm'.

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Удачи! = Good luck! (genitive: 'I wish you luck')
Secondary conversational sense ('success') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's a real stroke of luck.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'лыбнуться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to smile', paired with 'улыбаться'.

examples.text: Самсон, ну улыбнись. У нас мир.
examples.trans: Samson, come on, smile. We're at peace.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: movement by foot or figurative action

examples.text: Надо следить за каждым шагом соперника.
examples.trans: We must monitor every step of the rival.

examples.text: Надо следить за каждым шагом кандидата.
examples.trans: We must monitor every step of the candidate.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
